newsitem.title: USA: Josephine could be hurricane before Fla. landfall.
newsitem.headline: Josephine could be hurricane before Fla. landfall.

text.p: Tropical Storm Josephine rapidly gained strength and speed as it headed across the Gulf of Mexico Monday on a track that would take it ashore on Florida's Gulf coast, National Hurricane Center said.
Maximum sustained winds rose to 70 mph (112 kmh) Monday morning, a big increase from its previous 50 mph (80 kph), and forecasters said it was likely to become a hurricane before landfall.
A hurricane warning was in effect for Florida Gulf coast from the Anclote Keys to Apalachicola. A tropical storm warning was in effect south of the Anclote Keys to Fort Walton Beach, Fla.
Forecasters also issued a tropical storm warning for the U.S. East Coast from Cape Canaveral, Fla., to Little River Inlet, S.C.

At 1100 EDT/1500 GMT, Josephine's center was at latitude 27.6 north, longitude 86.6 west, about 175 miles (280 km) south-southwest of Apalachicola, and was moving northeast at 23 mph (37 kph), according to forecasters.
On its current track and speed, the center of the storm will move onshore sometime Monday night, but strong winds will reach the Florida coast hours earlier, forecasters said.

Tropical storm force winds extended outward about 175 miles (280 km) from the center, mainly to the southeast. Rainfall of up to five inches (13 cm) was possible along the track of the storm, along with strong onshore winds and coastal storm surge flooding of 6-9 feet (2-3 meters).

The Hurricane Center said weather in the Gulf was complicated by a strong pressure gradient between Josephine and high pressure to the north, which was causing strong winds elsewhere over the northern Gulf of Mexico.
